features.feature_value: Direct bullying/derisive wording flagged as a key negative cue driving stricter decisions
features.rationale: The participant explicitly cites bullying wording as influencing their keep/remove.

features.feature_value: Strongly linked profanity/foul language with immediate removal
features.rationale: They state foul language leads directly to instant removal.

features.feature_value: Personal discomfort with swearing and also with cruelty in opinions
features.evidence_span: "I don't agree with swearing and cursing"
features.rationale: They describe an attitude against cursing and cruelty that likely guided their judgments.

features.feature_value: Used civility and perceived one-sided derision/foulness as risk for 'bad blood'
features.rationale: They describe a concrete criterion (civility) and why posts that deride one side or use foul language were treated negatively.

features.feature_value: Seeing both versions together made them less likely to apply a double standard (would remove one side until seeing the other mirrored)
features.evidence_span: "Seeing both posts together like that definitely influenced my decision"
features.rationale: They explicitly attribute influence to the paired view and describe how it changed a prior bias.

features.feature_value: Only rejected content if it incited violence; otherwise inclined to allow both viewpoints
features.rationale: They set a safety-related threshold and state a permissive default when that condition isn’t present.

features.feature_value: Tried to keep posts with equal/respectful tone; removed ones described as hateful/filthy
features.rationale: They describe comparing tone/fairness across sides and removing content characterized as hateful.

features.feature_value: Recognized some statements as valid even when not personally agreeable
features.evidence_span: "There were alot of valid points being made"
features.rationale: They highlight reasoning validity despite disagreement, indicating the influence came from evaluating argument quality rather than agreement.
